title: Year-end 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC preparation: what to collect from the business
use_when: Use when the firm prepares a business client's Forms 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC for payments made in 2026; use payroll-new-contractor when collecting paperwork from one new contractor at the start of an engagement.
note: Built from IRS Publication 1099, General Instructions for Certain Information Returns (for use in preparing 2026 returns) and the Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (Rev. December 2026). For payments in tax years after 2025 most thresholds rose from $600 to $2,000; royalties stay at $10 and attorney gross proceeds at $600. It does not cover Forms 1099-K, 1042-S or W-2, state filing, or whether a worker is an employee.

i1099mec.name: IRS, Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (Rev. December 2026)

p1099.name: IRS, Publication 1099, General Instructions for Certain Information Returns (for use in preparing 2026 returns)

situations.rent: Did the business pay rent (other than to a real estate agent or property manager) of $2,000 or more to anyone?
situations.royalties: Did the business pay royalties of $10 or more?
situations.attorneys: Did the business pay a lawyer or law firm, including settlement payments made through a lawyer?
situations.medical: Did the business pay doctors or other health care providers in the course of its business?
situations.backup-withholding: Did the business withhold federal income tax (backup withholding) from any payee?
situations.tin-notices: Has the business received an IRS notice (CP2100 or similar) that a payee's name and TIN do not match?
situations.direct-sales: Did the business sell $5,000 or more of consumer products to anyone for resale outside a permanent retail store?

items.label: List of every person and business paid during the year, with full name and address
items.detail: Pub. 1099 part J: show the full name and address; for a sole proprietor, the individual's name first (a DBA may go on the second line); for a single-member disregarded LLC, the owner's name first.

items.label: Completed Form W-9 for each U.S. payee
items.detail: Pub. 1099 part J: the IRS suggests requesting Form W-9 to get the recipient's TIN. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Each payee's taxpayer identification number (SSN, ITIN or EIN)
items.detail: Instructions, Recipient's TIN. If a payee has not provided one, say so: the box is left blank and backup withholding may apply. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Whether each payee is an individual, partnership, LLC or corporation
items.detail: Instructions: payments to corporations are generally not reportable, except for legal services, medical and health care payments, and certain other payments listed under Reportable payments to corporations.

items.label: Form W-8 for each foreign payee
items.detail: Pub. 1099 part J: the IRS suggests requesting the appropriate Form W-8 from a foreign recipient. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Total paid to each non-employee for services during the year
items.detail: Form 1099-NEC, box 1a: nonemployee compensation of $2,000 or more, including fees, commissions, prizes and awards for services.

items.label: How each payment was made (check, ACH, cash, credit card, or a payment app such as a third-party network)
items.detail: Instructions, Form 1099-K: payments made by credit card, payment card or third-party network are reported by the payment settlement entity on Form 1099-K and are not reported on Form 1099-MISC or 1099-NEC.

items.label: Any cash tips or qualified overtime pay included in amounts paid to non-employees, with the payee's occupation
items.detail: New boxes 1b, 1c and 1d on Form 1099-NEC (and 13a, 13b and 14 on Form 1099-MISC) report cash tips, the Treasury Tipped Occupation Code and overtime compensation.

items.label: Rent paid to each landlord or equipment lessor
items.detail: Form 1099-MISC, box 1: $2,000 or more. Rent paid to a real estate agent or property manager is not reported by the business.

items.label: Royalties paid to each recipient
items.detail: Form 1099-MISC, box 2: at least $10, reported as gross royalties before reduction for fees, commissions or expenses.

items.label: Payments to lawyers and law firms, split between fees for legal services and settlement or other gross proceeds
items.detail: Attorney fees of $2,000 or more go in Form 1099-NEC box 1a; gross proceeds of $600 or more go in Form 1099-MISC box 10. The corporate exemption does not apply to legal services.

items.label: Payments to each physician or health care provider
items.detail: Form 1099-MISC, box 6: $2,000 or more, including payments to corporations.

items.label: Prizes, awards and other income payments not for services
Customers who bought $5,000 or more of consumer products for resale
items.detail: Form 1099-NEC box 2 or Form 1099-MISC box 7 (checkbox only, no dollar amount).

items.label: Federal income tax withheld from each payee under backup withholding
items.detail: Form 1099-MISC box 4 / Form 1099-NEC; Pub. 1099 part N says backup withholding is reported on Form 945 and on the 1099 even if the payment is below the reporting threshold.

items.label: Copies of IRS incorrect name/TIN notices (CP2100) and any B notices sent to payees
items.detail: Pub. 1099 part N; and the instructions' 2nd TIN Not. box, used when the IRS notified the payer twice within 3 calendar years.

items.label: Any new certified Form W-9 received from a payee after an IRS notice
items.detail: Pub. 1099 part N: stop withholding within 30 days after receiving a certified Form W-9. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.
